idea-plugin.name: Commit Hike
idea-plugin.description:
Every commit you make moves you along a hiking trail, right inside your IDE. A day of steady work takes you about ten kilometers along a real mountain ridge, a desert crossing or a folk tale, with a scene that changes as you go, a map, stories, facts and achievements.

  • Real trails. Ten routes: the Chornohora ridge over Hoverla, the Tongariro Alpine Crossing, the Tour du Mont Blanc and the Camino Francés on their real GPS tracks, Santiago's road from The Alchemist, folk tales and original stories, in two series you can walk one after another.
  • A hike you can watch. A side-on scene that follows the real elevation, the weather, the season and your clock, a minimap and a topographic map you zoom like paper. Look back at the way you came; what lies ahead stays hidden until you get there.
  • Real distances, your difficulty. A typical day of commits is about 10 km on medium (12.5 on easy, 8 on hard).
  • Stories, facts and achievements at every stop, streaks, days off, your year in a calendar and a passport with a stamp for every stop.
  • Share it. A postcard of where you are, saved, copied or posted to X, Bluesky, Mastodon, Threads, LinkedIn, Facebook, Telegram or Reddit with the text ready, and an SVG badge for your GitHub profile.
  • Walk together. Everyone committing to a project on the same trail, with a leaderboard, the team's week and a team goal: a route you walk together, everyone's commits adding up.
  • Five languages. English, Ukrainian, Polish, German and Spanish.
  • Routes from the site: Tools → Commit Hike → Routes from the Site… finds routes other walkers made on commit-hike.dev; install them with one click, and update them when their authors publish new versions.

Private by design. Nothing is written to your projects (no git hooks, no files): Commit Hike only reads git history. No accounts, no telemetry: the plugin connects only to commit-hike.dev, and only when you open Routes from the site or install a route (reading the public catalogue, sending nothing about you); Share opens a network's page in your browser only when you pick it. Lock files, generated code, whitespace-only changes and other people's commits don't count.

Open the Commit Hike tool window to see your trail; the status bar shows how far you've walked, and Tools | Commit Hike has everything else. The same progress also shows in your shell prompt and in Neovim: docs/terminal.md.

Read about it in English, Українською, po polsku, auf Deutsch or en español.
